admission.justification: Weighed four delivery architectures against measured host-bridge saturation and constrains future reset-scheduler concurrency, pool sizing, and documentation changes.

alternatives.option: Deliver due recipients through a fixed 16-worker reset pool (RESET_WORKERS = 16) backed by a durable SQLite reset index, accepting the measured physical ceiling of roughly 300 due recipients within 30 seconds and roughly 11 recipients per second beyond it.
alternatives.reason: Keeps peak concurrency bounded independently of fleet size, clears up to roughly 300 simultaneous resets within 30 seconds, drains larger backlogs steadily without starving the 4-thread ar-background pool, and matches the host-bridge saturation measurements.

alternatives.option: Keep serial delivery on the ordinary 15-second rotating receipt sweep (32 receipts per tick).
alternatives.reason: A backlog exceeding 32 waiting receipts or aged past the 24-hour / 512-entry held-receipt queue delays post-reset delivery across multiple sweep ticks past the 30-second requirement.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Fleet size stays permanently within a single 32-receipt sweep slice and 15-second sweep latency becomes acceptable.

alternatives.option: Raise RESET_WORKERS above 16 (such as 32 workers) or scale thread count with fleet size.
alternatives.reason: Host-bridge saturation limits throughput near 11 recipients per second at 16 workers, so raising thread count adds contention without materially shortening large-backlog drain times.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Host-bridge concurrency characteristics change so more than 16 worker threads increase sustained delivery throughput without exhausting host resources.

alternatives.option: Rewrite the host-bridge delivery protocol to eliminate per-recipient round-trip cost so unbounded simultaneous backlogs finish within 30 seconds.
alternatives.reason: Requires an invasive cross-process host-bridge redesign outside the leaf's scope when the measured 300-recipient / 11-per-second ceiling satisfies operational needs.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Production workloads regularly hit more than 300 simultaneous provider-limit resets and the ~11 recipients/second drain rate becomes operationally unacceptable.

consequences: Peak reset-delivery concurrency stays fixed at 16 threads independent of fleet size.
Up to roughly 300 simultaneous due recipients clear within 30 seconds of reset, and larger backlogs drain at roughly 11 recipients per second.
Operator documentation (docs/reference/mcp-tools.md) explicitly states the 16-worker pool, the ~300 / ~11-per-second D987 Option A ceiling, and the 512-entry / 24-hour queue bound.
context: Simultaneous provider-limit resets across large fleets require delivering waiting held messages promptly without leaving recipients behind the bounded 32-receipt ordinary sweep rotation, while host-bridge per-recipient execution cost caps sustained throughput.
decider: Developer (D987 Option A, 2026-11-25T09:09Z) following Architect ruling
